panels.title: Peers
panels.description: Total, inbound and outbound connection counts. The address-family and node-type splits are broken out on the connection-composition panels below, so plotting all eight overlapping slices here just made the totals hard to read.

panels.title: Known Addresses
panels.description: Size of the address manager's peer database. Split out because it is roughly 600x the connection count, so on a shared axis it hid every connection series.

panels.title: Peer Pings
panels.description: Round-trip ping latency to peers at the lower bound, median and upper bound, in microseconds. The series come from ping_us, so they are microseconds; the previous nanosecond unit made every reading a thousand times too large.

panels.title: Reject Messages Sent
panels.description: Reject messages sent, stacked by reason. The per-reason series are mutually exclusive and sum to the 'all rejects' series, so a stack shows both the total rejection rate and its composition. As nineteen unstacked bars this was unreadable. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.

Outbound connects and disconnects per second. Inbound accepted is also plotted but that counter is not in the current build; the two outbound series carry the churn signal. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Connection Churn

panels.description: Closes split by connection type. Listed explicitly because a wildcard would also match each type's .lifetimeSeconds sibling. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Connections Closed by Type

panels.description: Average lifetime at close, per type. A flood of one-second block-relay closes looks nothing like normal churn, and neither was visible before. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Connection Lifetime at Close

panels.description: Inbound evictions per second on the left axis, with the age of the evicted connection on the right. The age is in seconds and is one to two orders of magnitude larger than the eviction rate. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Inbound Evictions

panels.description: Inbound slot usage against the configured maximum, with total connections for context. The slot gauges are not in the current build, so only total connections plots today. Awaiting data: the currently deployed node build does not emit this metric yet, though the query matches the instrumentation in the source tree.
panels.title: Inbound Capacity

panels.description: Connections by type as a stacked area. The types are mutually exclusive and sum to the connection total, so the stack height is the peer count. panels.title: Peers by Connection Type

panels.description: Connections by transport protocol as a stacked area: cleartext v1, BIP324 v2 and peers still being probed. The band height is the connection total. panels.title: Peers by Transport Protocol

panels.description: Age of the oldest and newest connection. A newest age stuck near zero means constant churn; oldest age tracks how long the longest-lived peer has been with us. panels.title: Connection Age
